scheme_name: Scheme of Extending Family Maintenance Grant to the Families of the Deceased Famous Artists
description:
The Scheme of Extending Family Maintenance Grant to the Families of the Deceased Famous Artists was initiated by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to the families of renowned artists who have passed away. 

This scheme was launched in the year 2012. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to ensure that the families of deceased famous artists receive a monthly financial grant to support their livelihood. 

The financial assistance aims to alleviate the economic burden faced by these families after the loss of their primary earners. 

The scheme specifically targets families of artists who have made significant contributions to the fields of music, dance, drama, and other performing arts. 

Eligible artists must have been recognized for their contributions at a national or state level. 

The financial grant provided under this scheme is set at INR 5,000 per month. 

This amount is intended to provide a basic level of financial support to the families. 

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and aims to cover a wide range of artistic disciplines. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include that the deceased artist must have been a resident of India. 

Additionally, the artist must have been active in their field for a minimum of ten years prior to their death. 

The application process for the family maintenance grant requires the submission of specific documents. 

Families must provide a death certificate of the deceased artist. 

They must also submit proof of the artist's contributions to their field, such as awards or recognitions received. 

An application form must be filled out, detailing the family’s financial situation. 

The application form can typically be obtained from the Ministry of Culture or relevant state cultural departments. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the respective state government’s cultural department. 

The processing of applications usually takes around three months from the date of submission. 

Families are encouraged to apply as soon as possible after the artist's death to ensure timely assistance. 

The grant is disbursed on a monthly basis. 

The first payment is typically made within one month of the application approval. 

Subsequent payments are made on the first of every month thereafter. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this scheme. 

They are responsible for the verification of applications and the disbursement of funds. 

The Ministry of Culture can be contacted for more information regarding the scheme. 

Their official website provides additional resources and contact details for inquiries. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to support the arts and culture sector in India. 

It recognizes the significant impact that artists have on society and the economy. 

By providing financial support, the government aims to honor the legacy of these artists. 

The scheme also serves to encourage the continuation of artistic pursuits within families. 

In addition to financial support, the scheme aims to raise awareness about the contributions of artists to Indian culture. 

It highlights the need for ongoing support for the arts, especially in times of personal loss. 

The grant is not intended to replace other forms of income or support that the family may receive. 

It is specifically designed to provide additional financial security. 

The scheme has been positively received by many families of deceased artists. 

It has provided much-needed relief during difficult times. 

The government has also emphasized the importance of cultural heritage in its broader policies. 

This scheme is one of several initiatives aimed at preserving and promoting Indian arts and culture. 

The impact of this scheme can be seen in the lives of many families who have benefited from the financial assistance. 

The government continues to evaluate and improve the scheme based on feedback from beneficiaries. 

Overall, the Scheme of Extending Family Maintenance Grant to the Families of the Deceased Famous Artists represents a commitment to supporting the arts community in India. 

It acknowledges the sacrifices made by artists and their families. 

The scheme is a vital component of the government's efforts to sustain cultural heritage. 

In conclusion, this welfare scheme is an essential initiative that provides financial support to the families of deceased famous artists. 

It aims to ensure that their contributions to society are remembered and honored through tangible assistance. 

The monthly grant of INR 5,000 serves as a lifeline for many families. 

The application process is straightforward and designed to be accessible. 

The involvement of both central and state governments ensures that the scheme reaches those in need effectively. 

The ongoing commitment to the arts through such schemes reflects the importance of cultural preservation in India. 

The Scheme of Extending Family Maintenance Grant to the Families of the Deceased Famous Artists is a testament to the value placed on artistic contributions in Indian society. 

It is an important step towards recognizing and supporting the families left behind by those who have enriched the cultural landscape of the nation.
